sentence: This project builds statistical methods that help scientists study the human microbiome and its role in health and disease.
This project builds a microscope that uses stimulated Raman scattering to image live cells with high sensitivity.
This project tests whether an endocrine therapy called Elacestrant lessens bone damage while still eliminating cancer cells in breast cancer bone metastases.
This project studies why colorectal cancer cells with a deficiency become sensitive to asparaginase, an enzyme that produces ammonia.
This project uses long-read genome sequencing in a rat panel to find which DNA variants affect nicotine taking, withdrawal and nicotine seeking.
This project provides stem cell-derived cell models and genetically-engineered mouse models for studying Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes.
This project studies how a cytokine linked to allergic disease is made in lung lesions and how it shapes myeloid cells.
This project builds tools that harmonize brain images from multiple sites and combine data types to analyze preclinical Alzheimer's disease.
This project tries to find chemical marks called N6-methyladenosine on RNA that are linked to lung cancer risk, and the genes they affect.
This project builds deep learning tools that outline radiation therapy target volumes in head and neck cancer, while accounting for differences between observers.
This project studies how genome rearrangements happen in cancer and how shortened telomeres prevent tumors.
This project sets up a core facility that offers mouse models and 3D tumor spheroids for pre-clinical study of cancer.
This project studies how proteins that divide mitochondria affect the number, size and function of platelets.
This project provides primary human hepatocyte models to study why gene therapy for hemophilia A is not sustained.
This project studies genetic and epigenetic risk markers in autism and developmental delay, using a smartphone application that lets families take part.
This project builds machine learning and deep learning tools that combine many kinds of biomedical data to model disease and healthy states.
This project studies how one regulator protein guides blood precursor cells into T cells, and how that differs from its role in leukemia.
This project studies why dopaminergic neurons in the human midbrain are vulnerable to age-related oxidative stress, using human and non-human primate stem cell-derived neurons.
This project aims to find better treatments for blood diseases and to understand them.
This project develops monoclonal antibodies that mimic a T cell receptor to target human cancers.
